name: OpenLeverage RewardVault initialize() callable again through the delegator
summary: RewardVault.initialize(admin, distributor, expireDuration) has no initialized guard, and the RewardVaultDelegator forwards unknown calls to it, so anyone could rewrite the delegator's admin. The attacker called initialize to make its contract admin, used the delegator's setImplementation to point it at that contract, and through the new implementation swept the vault's own BABY and the RACA, BUSD, FLOKI, OLE and CSIX of five users who had approved the vault, selling all for 37.1 BNB.
notes: Anchored on the first initialize call after the constructor's (rule 10); the attacker's implementation is attack code, not a reset. The delegator kept the original admin and implementation 0x3d11015d from creation until the anchor, and no direct initialize call precedes it. The 649 later calls through the installed backdoor (from 0xf1e73123 and one other sender, blocks 44691790-44694665) moved no tokens.

This is a different defect from the OpenLeverage OPBorrowing incident (eip155:56:0xf78a85eb32a193e3ed2e708803b57ea8ea22a7f25792851e3de2d7945e6d02d5). Loss is the vault's and the five approvers' token outflow.
